BIOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Taxonomy I ● Meaning and significance of taxonomy ● Taxonomic units and nomencla? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Taxonomy I ● Meaning and significance of taxonomy ● Taxonomic units and nomencla.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Taxonomy I ● Meaning and significance of taxonomy ● Taxonomic units and nomencla.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Taxonomy I ● Meaning and significance of taxonomy ● Taxonomic units and nomencla.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Taxonomy I ● Meaning and significance of taxonomy ● Taxonomic units and nomencla.

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.

6. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in Plants ● Asexual reproduction (Sporulation and vegetative propag? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in Plants ● Asexual reproduction (Sporulation and vegetative propag.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in Plants ● Asexual reproduction (Sporulation and vegetative propag.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in Plants ● Asexual reproduction (Sporulation and vegetative propag.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in Plants ● Asexual reproduction (Sporulation and vegetative propag.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in Animals ● External fertilisation in animals ● Types of internal ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in Animals ● External fertilisation in animals ● Types of internal .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in Animals ● External fertilisation in animals ● Types of internal .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in Animals ● External fertilisation in animals ● Types of internal .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in Animals ● External fertilisation in animals ● Types of internal .

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Taxonomy II ● Kingdom Plantae (general characteristics of organisms in Divisions? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Taxonomy II ● Kingdom Plantae (general characteristics of organisms in Divisions.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Taxonomy II ● Kingdom Plantae (general characteristics of organisms in Divisions.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Taxonomy II ● Kingdom Plantae (general characteristics of organisms in Divisions.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Taxonomy II ● Kingdom Plantae (general characteristics of organisms in Divisions.

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growth and Development in Animals ● Metamorphosis (complete and incomplete metam? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Growth and Development in Animals ● Metamorphosis (complete and incomplete metam.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growth and Development in Animals ● Metamorphosis (complete and incomplete metam.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growth and Development in Animals ● Metamorphosis (complete and incomplete metam.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growth and Development in Animals ● Metamorphosis (complete and incomplete metam.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Taxonomy I ● Meaning and significance of taxonomy ● Taxonomic units and nomencla and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Ecology ● Ecosystems ● Adaptations of organisms to different habitats (xerophyte and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Cell Division ● Meaning of cell division and structure of chromosomes ● Types of and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
